001: Has the location of your exhibition booth for this trade show been decided yet?
Yes, it's the most visible spot, right to the left as you enter through the entrance.
That's great. Considering the flow of visitors, that's quite advantageous.
It is. However, the booth next to us is a competitor, so we need to be a bit careful.
I see. In that case, we need to highlight the features of our products more clearly.
Yes, that's why we're thinking of increasing the time for demonstrations.
002: Have the brochures for the trade show been printed yet?
Not yet. We've just finished the final design check.
I see. You should place the order soon so it makes the deadline.
Yes, we plan to send the data to the printing company tomorrow.
That's reassuring. Please check once more for any typos or errors.
Understood. We'll have multiple people check it to be absolutely sure.
003: Is there anything missing for the trade show preparations?
Let's see. It looks like we're running low on business cards, so I think we'll prepare some more.
That's important. Also, do we have enough promotional giveaways to hand out?
Yes, we have five hundred prepared. However, I have a feeling they'll run out by the morning of the first day.
In that case, let's place an order for about two hundred more as backup.
Thank you. That would be a big help.
004: What time should I arrive at the venue for tomorrow's trade show?
The doors open at nine, so please arrive by eight, an hour early.
Understood. Then I'll leave home at seven thirty.
Please do. Once you arrive, please do a final check of the booth first.
Got it. I'll also make sure the exhibits are working properly.
Yes, that's the most important thing, so thank you.
005: Which product do you plan to feature as the main focus at this trade show?
It's our newly developed energy-efficient motor. That's the main attraction.
That sounds promising. Are you preparing to show it in action?
Yes, we have two demonstration sets ready.
Excellent. I'm looking forward to seeing the customers' reactions.
Yes, I really hope many people will be interested.
006: How do you plan to handle the follow-up after the trade show?
We plan to send a thank-you email to everyone we exchanged business cards with within three days.
That's quick and good. After all, a fast response is important.
Right. Also, we intend to send materials individually to those who showed particular interest.
In that case, I think it would go more smoothly to assign a person in charge for each one.
Yes, we're preparing things that way.
007: How did you arrange transportation to the trade show venue?
We chartered one bus for the entire staff.
That's a good idea. It makes the commute much easier.
Yes, and we can transport the equipment at the same time, so I think it's efficient.
I see. Then, is it okay if I meet you all there?
Yes, no problem. Please contact me once you arrive.
008: Has the budget for the trade show been finalized yet?
We have a rough figure, but there are still a few items we're adjusting.
I see. Which items haven't been decided yet?
The decoration costs for the venue and the additional equipment rental fees.
In that case, maybe you should leave a little more room in the budget.
Yes, I think I'll set aside some contingency funds just in case.
009: Have you prepared the survey forms to hand out at the trade show?
Yes, we've printed five hundred. The questions have also been finalized.
That's good to hear. Have you done anything to increase the response rate?
We plan to give a small gift to those who fill out the survey.
That's a good method. I'm sure many people will cooperate.
I hope so. It would be great to gather as much data as possible.
010: How do you define success for this trade show?
First, it's getting over three hundred business card exchanges.
That's a specific goal. Is there anything else?
Next, we want to turn at least three of those into business negotiations.
I see. To achieve that, the response at the booth will probably be key.
Yes, we want to make sure the entire staff handles it well.
